claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Palantir created the Forward Deployed Software Engineer role in the early 2010s and called it a Delta.
claims.quote: The “Forward Deployed Software Engineer” role was created at data mining giant Palantir in the early 2010s, and was named “Delta.”

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Palantir contrasts a Dev’s focus as one capability for many customers with a Delta’s focus as one customer and many capabilities.
claims.quote: You can think of a Dev’s focus as “one capability, many customers,” while a Delta’s focus is “one customer, many capabilities”.

claims.question: q2

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Ramp put FDEs in place 9 months ago and has around 15 FDEs in pods working according to four core operating principles.
claims.quote: Put in place 9 months ago, Ramp has around 15 FDEs in pods who work according to four core operating principles.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Startups use FDEs in the sales process when a customer is undecided, offering an FDE to help the customer integrate the product.
claims.quote: Basically, when a customer is undecided on whether they can effectively use a product, Sales offers to provide an FDE to help them successfully integrate it.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The source distinguishes FDEs from consultants by saying consultants make one-off recommendations while FDEs generally work with customers long-term.
claims.quote: FDEs are sometimes mistakenly thought of as consultants, but the difference between consultants and FDEs is that the former make one-off recommendations, whereas FDEs generally work with customers, long-term.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Palantir sends empowered engineers to integrate its software for customer value, and the article says contracting companies see faster integration progress than by doing it themselves.
claims.quote: By sending in empowered engineers whose mission is to integrate Palantir’s software in a way that delivers customer value, Palantir “kills two birds with one stone”: they don’t need to worry too much about internal bureaucracy because they are blissfully unaware of it, and they send a “startup-minded” dev for the integration with the mindset of “how can I get this to work”, not “what are reasons this won’t work.” Companies contracting with Palantir see faster progress in software integration than by doing it themselves.
